1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:exp-setup}
6	
7	We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across seven instruction-tuned and reasoning-specialized models on four reasoning domains, with more than 2,400 evaluation instances.
8	
9	\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{guo2025deepseekr1}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq}. Parameter counts range from 7B to 32B.
10	
11	\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n=204$) provides formal logic problems with gold first-order logic (FOL) annotations for the oracle control (\S\ref{sec:oracle}). ProofWriter~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n=600$) tests multi-step deductive reasoning at depth~5. LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n=200$) evaluates logical reasoning from standardized examinations. StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n=200$) covers commonsense multi-hop reasoning. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n=30$) and AIME 2024 ($n=22$) serve as operating-regime probes for the degenerate case ($C_0 < 5\%$).
12	
13	\paragraph{Parameters.} $K=12$ traces at sampling temperature $T=0.7$. Constraint extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}=0.3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:prompts}). Z3~\citep{demoura2008z3} timeout: 10 seconds per problem. Penalty weight $\alpha = 0.5$ in all experiments.
14	
15	\paragraph{Metrics.} Accuracy (\%), $\Delta = \text{SICA} - \text{SC}$ in percentage points (pp). Statistical significance via McNemar exact test at $\alpha = 0.05$; 95\% bootstrap confidence intervals from 10{,}000 resamples for datasets with $n \geq 200$.
16	
17	
18	\subsection{Main Results: A Regime-Dependent Effect}
19	\label{sec:main-results}
20	
21	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all model-dataset conditions sorted by SC baseline. SICA effectiveness depends sharply on the model's baseline accuracy regime, with a narrow Goldilocks zone as the only region of significant positive effect.
22	
23	\begin{table*}[t]
24	\centering
25	\small
26	\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all conditions sorted by SC accuracy. $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC in percentage points. $^b$In-context learning with gold FOL examples. $\dagger$\,$n < 100$ (suggestive only). \textbf{Bold $\Delta$}: $p < 0.05$ (McNemar exact test). Significance: {*}\,$p < 0.05$;\enspace{**}\,$p < 0.01$;\enspace{***}\,$p < 0.001$.}
27	\label{tab:main_results}
28	\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
29	\toprule
30	Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
31	\midrule
32	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
33	Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.0095{**} \\
34	\midrule
35	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%)}} \\
36	Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 51.00 & 51.50 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
37	Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 53.92 & 57.35 & $\mathbf{+3.43}$ & 0.039{*} \\
38	Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s42) & 204 & 54.41 & \textbf{59.31} & $\mathbf{+4.90}$ & 0.013{*} \\
39	Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 56.37 & 55.88 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
40	\midrule
41	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
42	LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 63.24 & 60.78 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
43	LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
44	Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & n.s. \\
45	Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.00 & 74.51 & $-$0.49 & n.s. \\
46	Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 203 & 77.34 & 76.85 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
47	Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 78.50 & 78.00 & $-$0.50 & 1.000 \\
48	Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.82 & \textbf{84.31} & $+$0.49 & n.s. \\
49	\midrule
50	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Degenerate ($C_0 < 5\%$)}} \\
51	QwQ-32B & AIME 2024$^\dagger$ & 22 & 72.70 & 72.70 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
52	Qwen2.5-14B & GSM8K$^\dagger$ & 30 & 96.67 & 96.67 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
53	\midrule
54	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold FOL/DSL + Z3)}} \\
55	Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & \textbf{89.71} & $\mathbf{+14.22}$ & $2.0{\times}10^{-7}${***} \\
56	Qwen2.5-14B & ProofWriter & 600 & 75.17 & \textbf{86.67} & $\mathbf{+11.50}$ & $9.21{\times}10^{-15}${***} \\
57	\bottomrule
58	\end{tabular}
59	\end{table*}
60	
61	In the Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%), SICA provides significant gains on FOLIO. Mistral-7B achieves $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, McNemar $b = 12$, $c = 2$): 12 problems flip from incorrect to correct while only 2 flip in the reverse direction. A second seed replicates this effect at $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.039$); the third seed shows no effect ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp, $p = 1.0$; see \S\ref{sec:replication}). Mistral-7B on LogiQA (SC $= 51.00\%$), despite falling in the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$). Section~\ref{sec:failure-modes} attributes this to domain formalizability.
62	
63	\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%): confirmation bias.} Seven conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 1{,}600$) produce $|\Delta| \leq 2.45$\,pp, all nonsignificant. Qwen2.5-14B on two powered datasets (FOLIO $n = 204$, LogiQA $n = 200$) yields $|\Delta| \leq 0.50$\,pp. Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples (SC $= 74.37\%$, $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, $n = 199$) fails to break the pattern: improving extraction quality through exemplars does not overcome confirmation bias when the model already produces consistent traces. Qwen3-14B (SC $= 83.82\%$) represents a generational capability improvement yet produces $\Delta = +0.49$\,pp ($p > 0.05$).
64	
65	\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter depth-5 ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.0095$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} performance. Constraints extracted from predominantly incorrect traces encode wrong reasoning as formal rules, and the solver amplifies these errors rather than correcting them.
66	
67	\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$ (QwQ-32B on AIME 2024, Qwen2.5-14B on GSM8K), nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction. These probes confirm the $C_0$ diagnostic (\S\ref{sec:method}).
68	
69	Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence. The Goldilocks zone is narrow: the upper boundary is sharp (LLaMA-3.1-8B on FOLIO at SC $= 63.24\%$ already shows $\Delta = -2.45$\,pp), and below $\sim$40\% SC, constraints transition from noisy to actively harmful. The oracle rows (bottom of Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) confirm that gold constraints yield $\Delta = +14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), establishing that the aggregation mechanism is sound when constraints are discriminative (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).
70	
71	\begin{figure}[t]
72	\centering
73	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
74	\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline accuracy across all conditions. Filled markers: $n \geq 100$; open markers: $n < 100$. The Goldilocks zone (SC 50--55\%, shaded) contains the only significant positive effects. Type~A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): all nonsignificant ($|\Delta| \leq 2.45$\,pp). Type~C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): SICA significantly hurts ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p < 0.01$).}
75	\label{fig:regime-scatter}
76	\end{figure}
77	
78	
79	\subsection{Oracle Control: The Aggregation Mechanism Is Sound}
80	\label{sec:oracle}
81	
82	Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL formulas from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and domain-specific logic (DSL) programs from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). The oracle evaluates gold constraints against each candidate answer via Z3 directly; the scoring function (Eq.~\ref{eq:score}) remains unchanged. This design functions as a causal intervention on constraint quality while holding the aggregation mechanism constant.
83	
84	Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO versus 75.49\% for SC ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$, McNemar $b = 29$, $c = 0$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% of FOLIO problems (194/204). On ProofWriter, Oracle-SICA reaches 86.67\% versus 75.17\% ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$), with Z3 gold agreement of 97.1\% (577/594). Relational subtypes benefit most: RelNeg $+17.86$\,pp and RelNoneg $+13.01$\,pp (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:pw_oracle_subtype}).
85	
86	These results establish two conclusions. First, the MAX-SAT aggregation mechanism is sound: given discriminative constraints, it produces large and highly significant gains. Second, the gap between self-extraction and oracle performance quantifies the independence bottleneck. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+4.90$\,pp) captures only 34.5\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling ($+14.22$\,pp). The remaining 65.5\% is lost to self-extraction quality. Section~\ref{sec:failure-modes} decomposes this loss into three distinct failure modes.
87	
88	
89	\subsection{Three-Seed Replication}
90	\label{sec:replication}
91	
92	The Goldilocks result rests on Mistral-7B FOLIO performance, so we replicate with three random seeds to assess stability. All three runs use identical hyperparameters ($K = 12$, $T = 0.7$, $T_{\text{ext}} = 0.3$) on the full FOLIO evaluation set ($n = 204$).
93	
94	Seed~42 produces $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, SC $= 54.41\%$). Seed~123 replicates both the direction and significance at $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.039$, SC $= 53.92\%$). Seed~456 shows no effect ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp, $p = 1.0$, SC $= 56.37\%$). Two of three seeds reach significance at $\alpha = 0.05$; the mean effect across seeds is $\Delta = +2.61$\,pp.
95	
96	The variance is informative. Seed~456 produces a slightly higher SC baseline (56.37\% vs.\ 53.92--54.41\%) and no SICA gain, consistent with the regime-dependence pattern: as SC rises toward the upper boundary of the Goldilocks zone, the improvement vanishes. Sampling noise at the regime boundary can push individual seeds across the transition, which makes the effect fragile by design rather than by accident. This seed-level sensitivity motivates the entropy-conditioned analysis in \S\ref{sec:entropy}, where per-problem answer entropy reveals that the aggregate $\Delta$ is driven by the high-entropy subpopulation within each run.
97	
98	
99	\subsection{Failure Mode Analysis}
100	\label{sec:failure-modes}
101	
102	The regime-dependent pattern in Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reflects three distinct failure modes of self-extracted symbolic constraints.
103	
104	\paragraph{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%).} Strong models produce consistent reasoning traces, and constraints extracted from those traces mirror the answer distribution. When most constraints support the same candidate, MAX-SAT excludes few clauses ($|\mathcal{C}^{\setminus}| \approx 0$), the penalty term in Eq.~\ref{eq:score} vanishes, and the scoring function degenerates to weighted vote counting (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). SICA and SC then produce identical predictions. The ablation in \S\ref{sec:ablation} confirms this empirically: on Qwen2.5-14B (FOLIO + ProofWriter, $n = 804$), MAX-SAT and count-only baselines agree on 803 of 804 predictions.
105	
106	\paragraph{Type B: non-formalizable domains.} LogiQA problems require pragmatic and contextual reasoning that resists clean FOL formalization. Mistral-7B on LogiQA achieves an extraction rate of 86.4\% (fraction of traces yielding at least one parseable constraint), but the resulting constraints have a contradiction rate of only 0.8\%. Without genuine logical tension between constraints from different traces, MAX-SAT cannot discriminate among candidates. The condition sits in the Goldilocks SC range (51.00\%) yet produces $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), confirming that the right accuracy regime is necessary but not sufficient for SICA to help.
107	
108	\paragraph{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%).} When model accuracy is low, the majority of traces reach incorrect answers. Constraints extracted from wrong traces encode incorrect reasoning as formal rules. Z3 treats these rules as soft clauses with weight proportional to their frequency, so the solver preferentially satisfies the wrong constraints and penalizes traces that happen to reach the correct answer. Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.0095$) demonstrates this effect: SICA converts a weak positive signal in trace diversity into a net negative by formalizing the errors.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across seven instruction-tuned and reasoning-specialized models on four reasoning domains, with more than 2,400 evaluation instances.

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{guo2025deepseekr1}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq}. Parameter counts range from 7B to 32B.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n=204$) provides formal logic problems with gold first-order logic (FOL) annotations for the oracle control (\S\ref{sec:oracle}). ProofWriter~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n=600$) tests multi-step deductive reasoning at depth~5. LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n=200$) evaluates logical reasoning from standardized examinations. StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n=200$) covers commonsense multi-hop reasoning. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n=30$) and AIME 2024 ($n=22$) serve as operating-regime probes for the degenerate case ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K=12$ traces at sampling temperature $T=0.7$. Constraint extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}=0.3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:prompts}). Z3~\citep{demoura2008z3} timeout: 10 seconds per problem. Penalty weight $\alpha = 0.5$ in all experiments.

\paragraph{Metrics.} Accuracy (\%), $\Delta = \text{SICA} - \text{SC}$ in percentage points (pp). Statistical significance via McNemar exact test at $\alpha = 0.05$; 95\% bootstrap confidence intervals from 10{,}000 resamples for datasets with $n \geq 200$.


\subsection{Main Results: A Regime-Dependent Effect}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all model-dataset conditions sorted by SC baseline. SICA effectiveness depends sharply on the model's baseline accuracy regime, with a narrow Goldilocks zone as the only region of significant positive effect.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all conditions sorted by SC accuracy. $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC in percentage points. $^b$In-context learning with gold FOL examples. $\dagger$\,$n < 100$ (suggestive only). \textbf{Bold $\Delta$}: $p < 0.05$ (McNemar exact test). Significance: {*}\,$p < 0.05$;\enspace{**}\,$p < 0.01$;\enspace{***}\,$p < 0.001$.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.0095{**} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 51.00 & 51.50 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 53.92 & 57.35 & $\mathbf{+3.43}$ & 0.039{*} \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s42) & 204 & 54.41 & \textbf{59.31} & $\mathbf{+4.90}$ & 0.013{*} \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 56.37 & 55.88 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 63.24 & 60.78 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & n.s. \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.00 & 74.51 & $-$0.49 & n.s. \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 203 & 77.34 & 76.85 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 78.50 & 78.00 & $-$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.82 & \textbf{84.31} & $+$0.49 & n.s. \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Degenerate ($C_0 < 5\%$)}} \\
QwQ-32B & AIME 2024$^\dagger$ & 22 & 72.70 & 72.70 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & GSM8K$^\dagger$ & 30 & 96.67 & 96.67 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold FOL/DSL + Z3)}} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & \textbf{89.71} & $\mathbf{+14.22}$ & $2.0{\times}10^{-7}${***} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & ProofWriter & 600 & 75.17 & \textbf{86.67} & $\mathbf{+11.50}$ & $9.21{\times}10^{-15}${***} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

In the Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%), SICA provides significant gains on FOLIO. Mistral-7B achieves $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, McNemar $b = 12$, $c = 2$): 12 problems flip from incorrect to correct while only 2 flip in the reverse direction. A second seed replicates this effect at $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.039$); the third seed shows no effect ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp, $p = 1.0$; see \S\ref{sec:replication}). Mistral-7B on LogiQA (SC $= 51.00\%$), despite falling in the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$). Section~\ref{sec:failure-modes} attributes this to domain formalizability.

\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%): confirmation bias.} Seven conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 1{,}600$) produce $|\Delta| \leq 2.45$\,pp, all nonsignificant. Qwen2.5-14B on two powered datasets (FOLIO $n = 204$, LogiQA $n = 200$) yields $|\Delta| \leq 0.50$\,pp. Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples (SC $= 74.37\%$, $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, $n = 199$) fails to break the pattern: improving extraction quality through exemplars does not overcome confirmation bias when the model already produces consistent traces. Qwen3-14B (SC $= 83.82\%$) represents a generational capability improvement yet produces $\Delta = +0.49$\,pp ($p > 0.05$).

\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter depth-5 ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.0095$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} performance. Constraints extracted from predominantly incorrect traces encode wrong reasoning as formal rules, and the solver amplifies these errors rather than correcting them.

\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$ (QwQ-32B on AIME 2024, Qwen2.5-14B on GSM8K), nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction. These probes confirm the $C_0$ diagnostic (\S\ref{sec:method}).

Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence. The Goldilocks zone is narrow: the upper boundary is sharp (LLaMA-3.1-8B on FOLIO at SC $= 63.24\%$ already shows $\Delta = -2.45$\,pp), and below $\sim$40\% SC, constraints transition from noisy to actively harmful. The oracle rows (bottom of Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) confirm that gold constraints yield $\Delta = +14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), establishing that the aggregation mechanism is sound when constraints are discriminative (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline accuracy across all conditions. Filled markers: $n \geq 100$; open markers: $n < 100$. The Goldilocks zone (SC 50--55\%, shaded) contains the only significant positive effects. Type~A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): all nonsignificant ($|\Delta| \leq 2.45$\,pp). Type~C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): SICA significantly hurts ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p < 0.01$).}
\label{fig:regime-scatter}
\end{figure}


\subsection{Oracle Control: The Aggregation Mechanism Is Sound}
\label{sec:oracle}

Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL formulas from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and domain-specific logic (DSL) programs from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). The oracle evaluates gold constraints against each candidate answer via Z3 directly; the scoring function (Eq.~\ref{eq:score}) remains unchanged. This design functions as a causal intervention on constraint quality while holding the aggregation mechanism constant.

Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO versus 75.49\% for SC ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$, McNemar $b = 29$, $c = 0$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% of FOLIO problems (194/204). On ProofWriter, Oracle-SICA reaches 86.67\% versus 75.17\% ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$), with Z3 gold agreement of 97.1\% (577/594). Relational subtypes benefit most: RelNeg $+17.86$\,pp and RelNoneg $+13.01$\,pp (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:pw_oracle_subtype}).

These results establish two conclusions. First, the MAX-SAT aggregation mechanism is sound: given discriminative constraints, it produces large and highly significant gains. Second, the gap between self-extraction and oracle performance quantifies the independence bottleneck. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+4.90$\,pp) captures only 34.5\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling ($+14.22$\,pp). The remaining 65.5\% is lost to self-extraction quality. Section~\ref{sec:failure-modes} decomposes this loss into three distinct failure modes.


\subsection{Three-Seed Replication}
\label{sec:replication}

The Goldilocks result rests on Mistral-7B FOLIO performance, so we replicate with three random seeds to assess stability. All three runs use identical hyperparameters ($K = 12$, $T = 0.7$, $T_{\text{ext}} = 0.3$) on the full FOLIO evaluation set ($n = 204$).

Seed~42 produces $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, SC $= 54.41\%$). Seed~123 replicates both the direction and significance at $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.039$, SC $= 53.92\%$). Seed~456 shows no effect ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp, $p = 1.0$, SC $= 56.37\%$). Two of three seeds reach significance at $\alpha = 0.05$; the mean effect across seeds is $\Delta = +2.61$\,pp.

The variance is informative. Seed~456 produces a slightly higher SC baseline (56.37\% vs.\ 53.92--54.41\%) and no SICA gain, consistent with the regime-dependence pattern: as SC rises toward the upper boundary of the Goldilocks zone, the improvement vanishes. Sampling noise at the regime boundary can push individual seeds across the transition, which makes the effect fragile by design rather than by accident. This seed-level sensitivity motivates the entropy-conditioned analysis in \S\ref{sec:entropy}, where per-problem answer entropy reveals that the aggregate $\Delta$ is driven by the high-entropy subpopulation within each run.


\subsection{Failure Mode Analysis}
\label{sec:failure-modes}

The regime-dependent pattern in Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reflects three distinct failure modes of self-extracted symbolic constraints.

\paragraph{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%).} Strong models produce consistent reasoning traces, and constraints extracted from those traces mirror the answer distribution. When most constraints support the same candidate, MAX-SAT excludes few clauses ($|\mathcal{C}^{\setminus}| \approx 0$), the penalty term in Eq.~\ref{eq:score} vanishes, and the scoring function degenerates to weighted vote counting (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). SICA and SC then produce identical predictions. The ablation in \S\ref{sec:ablation} confirms this empirically: on Qwen2.5-14B (FOLIO + ProofWriter, $n = 804$), MAX-SAT and count-only baselines agree on 803 of 804 predictions.

\paragraph{Type B: non-formalizable domains.} LogiQA problems require pragmatic and contextual reasoning that resists clean FOL formalization. Mistral-7B on LogiQA achieves an extraction rate of 86.4\% (fraction of traces yielding at least one parseable constraint), but the resulting constraints have a contradiction rate of only 0.8\%. Without genuine logical tension between constraints from different traces, MAX-SAT cannot discriminate among candidates. The condition sits in the Goldilocks SC range (51.00\%) yet produces $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), confirming that the right accuracy regime is necessary but not sufficient for SICA to help.

\paragraph{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%).} When model accuracy is low, the majority of traces reach incorrect answers. Constraints extracted from wrong traces encode incorrect reasoning as formal rules. Z3 treats these rules as soft clauses with weight proportional to their frequency, so the solver preferentially satisfies the wrong constraints and penalizes traces that happen to reach the correct answer. Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.0095$) demonstrates this effect: SICA converts a weak positive signal in trace diversity into a net negative by formalizing the errors.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across seven instruction-tuned and reasoning-specialized models on four reasoning domains, with more than 2,400 evaluation instances.

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{guo2025deepseekr1}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq}. Parameter counts range from 7B to 32B.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n=204$) provides formal logic problems with gold first-order logic (FOL) annotations for the oracle control (\S\ref{sec:oracle}). ProofWriter~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n=600$) tests multi-step deductive reasoning at depth~5. LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n=200$) evaluates logical reasoning from standardized examinations. StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n=200$) covers commonsense multi-hop reasoning. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n=30$) and AIME 2024 ($n=22$) serve as operating-regime probes for the degenerate case ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K=12$ traces at sampling temperature $T=0.7$. Constraint extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}=0.3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:prompts}). Z3~\citep{demoura2008z3} timeout: 10 seconds per problem. Penalty weight $\alpha = 0.5$ in all experiments.

\paragraph{Metrics.} Accuracy (\%), $\Delta = \text{SICA} - \text{SC}$ in percentage points (pp). Statistical significance via McNemar exact test at $\alpha = 0.05$; 95\% bootstrap confidence intervals from 10{,}000 resamples for datasets with $n \geq 200$.


\subsection{Main Results: A Regime-Dependent Effect}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all model-dataset conditions sorted by SC baseline. SICA effectiveness depends sharply on the model's baseline accuracy regime, with a narrow Goldilocks zone as the only region of significant positive effect.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all conditions sorted by SC accuracy. $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC in percentage points. $^b$In-context learning with gold FOL examples. $\dagger$\,$n < 100$ (suggestive only). \textbf{Bold $\Delta$}: $p < 0.05$ (McNemar exact test). Significance: {*}\,$p < 0.05$;\enspace{**}\,$p < 0.01$;\enspace{***}\,$p < 0.001$.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.0095{**} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 51.00 & 51.50 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 53.92 & 57.35 & $\mathbf{+3.43}$ & 0.039{*} \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s42) & 204 & 54.41 & \textbf{59.31} & $\mathbf{+4.90}$ & 0.013{*} \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 56.37 & 55.88 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 63.24 & 60.78 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & n.s. \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.00 & 74.51 & $-$0.49 & n.s. \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 203 & 77.34 & 76.85 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 78.50 & 78.00 & $-$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.82 & \textbf{84.31} & $+$0.49 & n.s. \\
\midrule

\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold FOL/DSL + Z3)}} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & \textbf{89.71} & $\mathbf{+14.22}$ & $2.0{\times}10^{-7}${***} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & ProofWriter & 600 & 75.17 & \textbf{86.67} & $\mathbf{+11.50}$ & $9.21{\times}10^{-15}${***} \\

In the Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%), SICA provides significant gains on FOLIO. Mistral-7B achieves $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, McNemar $b = 12$, $c = 2$): 12 problems flip from incorrect to correct while only 2 flip in the reverse direction. A second seed replicates this effect at $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.039$); the third seed shows no effect ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp, $p = 1.0$; see \S\ref{sec:replication}). Mistral-7B on LogiQA (SC $= 51.00\%$), despite falling in the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$). Section~\ref{sec:failure-modes} attributes this to domain formalizability.

\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%): confirmation bias.} Seven conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 1{,}600$) produce $|\Delta| \leq 2.45$\,pp, all nonsignificant. Qwen2.5-14B on two powered datasets (FOLIO $n = 204$, LogiQA $n = 200$) yields $|\Delta| \leq 0.50$\,pp. Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples (SC $= 74.37\%$, $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, $n = 199$) fails to break the pattern: improving extraction quality through exemplars does not overcome confirmation bias when the model already produces consistent traces. Qwen3-14B (SC $= 83.82\%$) represents a generational capability improvement yet produces $\Delta = +0.49$\,pp ($p > 0.05$).

\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter depth-5 ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.0095$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} performance. Constraints extracted from predominantly incorrect traces encode wrong reasoning as formal rules, and the solver amplifies these errors rather than correcting them.

\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$ (QwQ-32B on AIME 2024, Qwen2.5-14B on GSM8K), nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction. These probes confirm the $C_0$ diagnostic (\S\ref{sec:method}).

Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence. The Goldilocks zone is narrow: the upper boundary is sharp (LLaMA-3.1-8B on FOLIO at SC $= 63.24\%$ already shows $\Delta = -2.45$\,pp), and below $\sim$40\% SC, constraints transition from noisy to actively harmful. The oracle rows (bottom of Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) confirm that gold constraints yield $\Delta = +14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), establishing that the aggregation mechanism is sound when constraints are discriminative (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline accuracy across all conditions. Filled markers: $n \geq 100$; open markers: $n < 100$. The Goldilocks zone (SC 50--55\%, shaded) contains the only significant positive effects. Type~A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): all nonsignificant ($|\Delta| \leq 2.45$\,pp). Type~C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): SICA significantly hurts ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p < 0.01$).}
\label{fig:regime-scatter}
\end{figure}


\subsection{Oracle Control: The Aggregation Mechanism Is Sound}
\label{sec:oracle}

Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL formulas from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and domain-specific logic (DSL) programs from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). The oracle evaluates gold constraints against each candidate answer via Z3 directly; the scoring function (Eq.~\ref{eq:score}) remains unchanged. This design functions as a causal intervention on constraint quality while holding the aggregation mechanism constant.

Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO versus 75.49\% for SC ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$, McNemar $b = 29$, $c = 0$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% of FOLIO problems (194/204). On ProofWriter, Oracle-SICA reaches 86.67\% versus 75.17\% ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$), with Z3 gold agreement of 97.1\% (577/594). Relational subtypes benefit most: RelNeg $+17.86$\,pp and RelNoneg $+13.01$\,pp (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:pw_oracle_subtype}).

These results establish two conclusions. First, the MAX-SAT aggregation mechanism is sound: given discriminative constraints, it produces large and highly significant gains. Second, the gap between self-extraction and oracle performance quantifies the independence bottleneck. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+4.90$\,pp) captures only 34.5\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling ($+14.22$\,pp). The remaining 65.5\% is lost to self-extraction quality. Section~\ref{sec:failure-modes} decomposes this loss into three distinct failure modes.


\subsection{Three-Seed Replication}
\label{sec:replication}

The Goldilocks result rests on Mistral-7B FOLIO performance, so we replicate with three random seeds to assess stability. All three runs use identical hyperparameters ($K = 12$, $T = 0.7$, $T_{\text{ext}} = 0.3$) on the full FOLIO evaluation set ($n = 204$).

Seed~42 produces $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, SC $= 54.41\%$). Seed~123 replicates both the direction and significance at $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.039$, SC $= 53.92\%$). Seed~456 shows no effect ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp, $p = 1.0$, SC $= 56.37\%$). Two of three seeds reach significance at $\alpha = 0.05$; the mean effect across seeds is $\Delta = +2.61$\,pp.

The variance is informative. Seed~456 produces a slightly higher SC baseline (56.37\% vs.\ 53.92--54.41\%) and no SICA gain, consistent with the regime-dependence pattern: as SC rises toward the upper boundary of the Goldilocks zone, the improvement vanishes. Sampling noise at the regime boundary can push individual seeds across the transition, which makes the effect fragile by design rather than by accident. This seed-level sensitivity motivates the entropy-conditioned analysis in \S\ref{sec:entropy}, where per-problem answer entropy reveals that the aggregate $\Delta$ is driven by the high-entropy subpopulation within each run.


\subsection{Failure Mode Analysis}
\label{sec:failure-modes}

The regime-dependent pattern in Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reflects three distinct failure modes of self-extracted symbolic constraints.

\paragraph{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%).} Strong models produce consistent reasoning traces, and constraints extracted from those traces mirror the answer distribution. When most constraints support the same candidate, MAX-SAT excludes few clauses ($|\mathcal{C}^{\setminus}| \approx 0$), the penalty term in Eq.~\ref{eq:score} vanishes, and the scoring function degenerates to weighted vote counting (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). SICA and SC then produce identical predictions. The ablation in \S\ref{sec:ablation} confirms this empirically: on Qwen2.5-14B (FOLIO + ProofWriter, $n = 804$), MAX-SAT and count-only baselines agree on 803 of 804 predictions.

\paragraph{Type B: non-formalizable domains.} LogiQA problems require pragmatic and contextual reasoning that resists clean FOL formalization. Mistral-7B on LogiQA achieves an extraction rate of 86.4\% (fraction of traces yielding at least one parseable constraint), but the resulting constraints have a contradiction rate of only 0.8\%. Without genuine logical tension between constraints from different traces, MAX-SAT cannot discriminate among candidates. The condition sits in the Goldilocks SC range (51.00\%) yet produces $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), confirming that the right accuracy regime is necessary but not sufficient for SICA to help.

\paragraph{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%).} When model accuracy is low, the majority of traces reach incorrect answers. Constraints extracted from wrong traces encode incorrect reasoning as formal rules. Z3 treats these rules as soft clauses with weight proportional to their frequency, so the solver preferentially satisfies the wrong constraints and penalizes traces that happen to reach the correct answer. Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.0095$) demonstrates this effect: SICA converts a weak positive signal in trace diversity into a net negative by formalizing the errors.

# Writing Plan — symb_invariant_consensus
# Generated: 2026-05-19T14:00:00Z
# Updated: 2026-05-19T16:00:00Z — D060: Method improvement failed → pure analysis paper
# Full Draft: Independence Bottleneck (Condorcet) — Analysis paper
# Paper Agent Step 1 output

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: main
  template: templates/latex/acl/
  template_note: "ACL template shared by EMNLP; confirm 2026 style options when official EMNLP 2026 CFP releases"
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  title: >
    Beyond Self-Consistency: How Trace Independence Limits
    Symbolic Consensus in LLM Reasoning
  core_claim: >
    Self-consistency's theoretical basis (Condorcet Jury Theorem) requires voter
    independence, but same-model sampling severely violates this assumption
    (Fleiss' κ = 0.40–0.74, Effective-K only 1.2–2.2 for nominal K=12). Oracle control
    (+14.22pp) proves the aggregation mechanism works, but self-extracted
    constraints capture only 35% of this ceiling. Nine remediation strategies
    spanning prompting, architecture, capability, verification, diversity, and
    filtering dimensions all fail, confirming the independence bottleneck is
    structural.
  paper_type: "Analysis paper (Condorcet theoretical framework + empirical diagnosis + 9 remediation failures)"
  framing: "Independence Bottleneck (Condorcet)"
  d060_note: "Method improvement (multi-temp, filtering, T=1.0) all failed → pure analysis"
  created_at: 2026-05-19T14:00:00Z
  updated_at: 2026-05-19T16:00:00Z

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contributions (4 verified)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
contributions:
  - id: C1
    label: "Independence Bottleneck"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence; same-model traces
      violate this (Mistral κ=0.41 Eff-K=2.17, Qwen κ=0.744 Eff-K=1.31).
      Effective-K quantifies how many truly independent traces K samples provide.
      Cross-seed κ stable (0.412 vs 0.401) but Δ unstable (+3.43 vs -0.49pp) →
      Eff-K is necessary but not sufficient.
    evidence: "§5.1, Table 3, Figure 3"

  - id: C2
    label: "Oracle Gap — Extraction Bottleneck"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      Gold FOL + MAX-SAT = +14.22pp (p=2.0e-7) FOLIO, +11.50pp PW. Self-extraction
      captures only 35% of oracle ceiling. Aggregation mechanism sound; extraction
      quality is the binding bottleneck.
    evidence: "§4.3, Table 1 (oracle rows)"

  - id: C3
    label: "Regime-Dependent Capability Trap"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      SICA effectiveness depends on model accuracy regime: Type A (SC≥~60%,
      confirmation bias), Type B (non-formalizable domain), Type C (SC≤~40%,
      noisy constraints, Δ=-2.83pp p=0.0095). Goldilocks zone (~50–55% SC)
      yields only significant gain (+4.90pp, p=0.013, 2/3 seeds significant at α=0.05).
    evidence: "§4.2, §4.4, §4.5, Table 1, Figure 2"

  - id: C4
    label: "C0+SC Deployment Diagnostic + K/T Sensitivity"
    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >
      C0 (multi-candidate rate) + SC accuracy forms zero-cost deployment diagnostic.
      K sensitivity shows inverted-U (K=12 sweet spot). T sensitivity shows effect
      fragility (T=0.7 +4.90pp → T=1.0 +0.55pp). Nine remediation strategies
      spanning all intervention dimensions fail, confirming structural bottleneck.
    evidence: "§5.3, §5.4, §5.5, Figure 3, Appendix remediation table"

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Paper Outline
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
paper_outline:
  - section: abstract
    file: abstract.tex
    word_budget: 220
    phase: 2
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem: SC (majority voting) plateaus; Condorcet Jury Theorem explains why — traces lack independence"
      - "Method: SICA pipeline, 7 models (7B–32B), 4 domains, N>2,400"
      - "Independence quantification: Fleiss' κ → Eff-K=1.20–2.17 at K=12"
      - "Regime-dependent effect: +4.90pp Goldilocks zone (2/3 seeds significant), -2.83pp Type C, ~0 Type A"
      - "Oracle +14.22pp/+11.50pp proves aggregation sound"
      - "9 remediation strategies all fail — bottleneck is structural"
      - "K sensitivity: inverted-U (K=12 sweet spot); T sensitivity: fragile (T=0.7→T=1.0 collapses)"
      - "C0+SC deployment diagnostic"
    dependencies: [experiments, analysis, method]

  - section: introduction
    file: introduction.tex
    word_budget: 1300
    phase: 2
    core_bullets:
      - "P1: Scaling test-time computation; SC as dominant aggregation; diminishing returns (Loo et al. 2025)"
      - "P2: Neuro-symbolic methods (Logic-LM, LINC, DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer) show gains but use external/trained components. Can same-model self-extraction suffice?"
      - "P3: Theoretical lens — Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence. Same-model traces violate this (Eff-K=1.20–2.17). Symbolic verification could inject independent signal, but self-extraction inherits trace non-independence."
      - "P4: Our approach — SICA pipeline + Condorcet analysis + 7 models × 4 domains + 3-seed replication. Core finding: independence bottleneck. 9 remediation strategies all fail."
      - "P5: Contributions (C1–C4)"
    dependencies: [experiments, analysis, method]
    figures: [fig1_pipeline]

  - section: related_work
    file: related_work.tex
    word_budget: 800
    phase: 1
    core_bullets:
      - "Cluster 1: SC and extensions — SC, USC, weighted SC, DiVeRSe, scaling plateaus"
      - "Cluster 2: Neuro-symbolic reasoning — Logic-LM, LINC, DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer, LogicAgent; key distinction: trained/external vs same-model self-extraction"
      - "Cluster 3: Test-time compute — Snell et al. 2025, DeepSeek-R1, diversity-aware TTS"
      - "Cluster 4: Verification and reranking — ORM, PRM, Math-Shepherd"
      - "Cluster 5: Condorcet/voting theory and ensemble diversity — Condorcet 1785, Austen-Smith & Banks 1996, arXiv:2409.00094 (closest prior work)"
    dependencies: []

  - section: method
    file: method.tex
    word_budget: 1200
    phase: 1
    subsections:
      - id: "sec:condorcet"
        title: "Self-Consistency and the Condorcet Independence Assumption"
        word_budget: 300
        bullets:
          - "SC as majority voting; Condorcet Jury Theorem: K independent voters with p>0.5 → correct majority as K→∞"
          - "LLM traces violate independence: same model, same prompt, only sampling temperature"
          - "Eff-K = K / (1 + (K-1)·κ) where κ = Fleiss' Kappa — effective independent voter count"
          - "When Eff-K ≈ 1, additional traces provide no new information"
      - id: "sec:sica-pipeline"
        title: "SICA Pipeline"
        word_budget: 450
        bullets:
          - "K-trace generation at T=0.7"
          - "FOL constraint extraction at T_ext=0.3 (in practice: predominantly ground propositional clauses)"
          - "Syntactic deduplication"
          - "Weighted partial MAX-SAT: hard clauses (answer assertion), soft clauses (constraints weighted by occurrence)"
          - "Z3 solver, 10s timeout per candidate; answer with highest satisfiable subset selected"
      - id: "sec:oracle-design"
        title: "Oracle Control Design"
        word_budget: 200
        bullets:
          - "Replace self-extracted constraints with gold FOL (FOLIO) / DSL (ProofWriter)"
          - "Z3 evaluates gold constraint against each candidate answer"
          - "Causal intervention: isolates constraint quality from aggregation mechanism"
      - id: "sec:scope"
        title: "Scope"
        word_budget: 100
        bullets:
          - "Same-model self-extraction pipeline"
          - "Methods using trained extractors / external provers out of scope"
    dependencies: []
    figures: [fig1_pipeline]

  - section: experiments
    file: experiments.tex
    word_budget: 1800
    phase: 1
    subsections:
      - id: "sec:exp-setup"
        title: "Experimental Setup"
        word_budget: 300
        bullets:
          - "7 models: Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-14B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, LLaMA-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B, QwQ-32B"
          - "4 domains: FOLIO (n=204), ProofWriter (n=600), LogiQA (n=200), StrategyQA (n=200/60)"
          - "Probes: GSM8K (n=30), AIME 2024 (n=22)"
          - "K=12, T=0.7, T_ext=0.3, Z3 timeout 10s"
          - "Metrics: accuracy (%), Δ=SICA−SC (pp), McNemar exact test α=0.05, 95% bootstrap CIs"
      - id: "sec:main-results"
        title: "Main Results: A Regime-Dependent Effect"
        word_budget: 450
        bullets:
          - "Table 1: all conditions sorted by SC%, grouped by regime"
          - "Goldilocks zone (~50–55% SC): Mistral FOLIO +4.90pp p=0.013 (b=12,c=2)"
          - "Type A (SC≥~60%): 8+ conditions, all n.s., combined N>2,000"
          - "Type C (SC≤~40%): Mistral PW-600 Δ=-2.83pp p=0.0095 — SICA hurts"
          - "Degenerate: C0<5% (QwQ, GSM8K) → SICA≡SC"
        data_source: "registry: exp-033, exp-046, exp-041, exp-026, exp-035, exp-038, exp-020, exp-027, exp-019, exp-044b, exp-050b, exp-049b, exp-014, exp-017, exp-012, sica_aime30_v3"
      - id: "sec:oracle"
        title: "Oracle Control: Aggregation Is Sound"
        word_budget: 300
        bullets:
          - "FOLIO: oracle-SICA 89.71% vs SC 75.49% (+14.22pp, p=2.0e-7, b=29, c=0)"
          - "ProofWriter: oracle-SICA 86.67% vs SC 75.17% (+11.50pp, p=9.21e-15)"
          - "Z3 gold agreement: 95.1% FOLIO, 97.1% PW"
          - "Best self-extraction captures 34.5% of oracle ceiling"
        data_source: "registry: exp-031, exp-022"
      - id: "sec:replication"
        title: "Three-Seed Replication"
        word_budget: 250
        bullets:
          - "Mistral-7B FOLIO-204: seeds 42/123/456"
          - "Seed 42 (exp-033): Δ=+4.90pp p=0.013"
          - "Seed 123 (exp-052): Δ=+3.43pp p=0.039"
          - "Seed 456 (exp-053): Δ=-0.49pp p=1.0"
          - "2/3 seeds significant at α=0.05; mean Δ=+2.61pp"
          - "Variance across seeds highlights sensitivity to sampling → motivates independence analysis"
        data_source: "registry: exp-033, exp-052, exp-053"
      - id: "sec:failure-modes"
        title: "Failure Mode Analysis"
        word_budget: 300
        bullets:
          - "Type A: strong models → consistent traces → constraints mirror answers → MAX-SAT = counting"
          - "Type B: non-formalizable domain (LogiQA: extraction rate 86.4%, contradiction rate 0.8%)"
          - "Type C: wrong traces → wrong constraints → solver amplifies errors"
    dependencies: []
    tables: [tab1_main_results]
    figures: [fig2_regime_scatter]

  - section: analysis
    file: analysis.tex
    word_budget: 1500
    phase: 1
    subsections:
      - id: "sec:effective-k"
        title: "Condorcet Effective-K Analysis"
        word_budget: 350
        bullets:
          - "Fleiss' κ per model-domain condition from K=12 trace answer distributions"
          - "Eff-K = K / (1 + (K-1)·κ)"
          - "Mistral FOLIO: κ=0.412 (s123) / 0.401 (s456), Eff-K=2.17 / 2.22 (highest diversity)"
          - "Qwen-14B FOLIO: κ=0.744, Eff-K=1.31 (most redundant)"
          - "Qwen-14B LogiQA: κ=0.821, Eff-K=1.20 (lowest Eff-K)"
          - "Cross-seed κ stable (0.412 vs 0.401) but Δ unstable (+3.43 vs -0.49pp) → Eff-K necessary not sufficient"
          - "Correlation: higher Eff-K → more room for SICA gain"
          - "Explains SC plateau: adding traces beyond Eff-K provides no new information"
        data_source: "comp-1 Worker output (Fleiss' κ from per-problem trace data)"
      - id: "sec:extraction-taxonomy"
        title: "Extraction Error Taxonomy"
        word_budget: 250
        bullets:
          - "Discriminative rate: ~8% Z3-discriminative (95% CI [7.6, 8.8])"
          - "Even removing non-discriminative constraints provides zero gain (filtering experiment)"
          - "Variable naming inconsistency: 56.4% constraint pairs share zero Z3 variables"
          - "Self-extraction captures ~18% of oracle quality"
        data_source: "registry: exp-023, exp-036b; filtering validation data"
        note: "D060: 43.1% trivially_satisfied number under review — use verified ~8% non-discriminative framing"
      - id: "sec:k-sensitivity"
        title: "K Sensitivity"
        word_budget: 250
        bullets:
          - "Inverted-U curve: K=4 Δ=-1.47pp, K=8 Δ=-0.98pp, K=12 Δ=+4.90pp, K=16 Δ=+1.47pp"
          - "K=12 is sweet spot; K=4 SC ≈ K=12 SC but SICA differs by ~6.4pp"
          - "Proves SICA extracts different information than SC at sufficient K"
          - "Links to Eff-K: diminishing returns from non-independent traces"
          - "K=20 pending"
        data_source: "Director K sensitivity data; registry: exp-051"
      - id: "sec:t-sensitivity"
        title: "Temperature Sensitivity"
        word_budget: 100
        bullets:
          - "T=0.7: Δ=+4.90pp (exp-033); T=1.0: Δ=+0.55pp (exp-054)"
          - "Effect extremely fragile to temperature — higher T increases diversity but degrades trace quality"
        data_source: "registry: exp-033, exp-054"
      - id: "sec:entropy"
        title: "Entropy-Conditioned Mechanism"
        word_budget: 200
        bullets:
          - "Per-problem answer entropy mediates SICA effectiveness"
          - "Mistral: low Δ=0, med Δ=+4.5, high Δ=+9.6pp (monotonic)"
          - "Proportion of high-entropy problems: Mistral 35.8% vs Qwen 10.3%"
          - "Causal chain: strong model → consistent traces → low entropy → redundant constraints"
        data_source: "registry: exp-033 per_entropy, exp-026"
      - id: "sec:ablation"
        title: "Constraint Ablation"
        word_budget: 100
        bullets:
          - "MAX-SAT vs count-only: 803/804 agree (Qwen-14B, n=804)"
          - "Self-extracted constraints carry no signal beyond vote counts in high-SC regime"
        data_source: "registry: sica_constraint_ablation_013"
      - id: "sec:remediation"
        title: "Remediation Analysis"
        word_budget: 250
        bullets:
          - "9 strategies spanning 6 intervention dimensions, all fail:"
          - "  Prompting: contrastive extraction (exp-029: disc_rate 8.2%→6.0%, Δ=-1.1pp)"
          - "  Architecture: cross-model extraction (exp-030: 0% discriminative)"
          - "  Capability: generational scaling Qwen3 (exp-027: +0.49pp n.s.)"
          - "  Verification: Z3 feedback (exp-036: 0.9% UNSAT trigger), cross-trace UNSAT (exp-036b: 56.4% zero vars)"
          - "  Diversity: multi-temp sampling (n=28, Δ=0.00pp), T=1.0 (Δ=+0.55pp, collapse from +4.90pp)"
          - "  Filtering: discriminative constraint filtering (0 gain)"
          - "  Consistency: consistency filtering (exp-043: reverts to SC at T≥4)"
          - "All fail → independence bottleneck is structural, not addressable by prompt/solver/diversity interventions"
          - "1-paragraph summary in main text; full table in appendix"
        data_source: "registry: exp-029, exp-030, exp-027, exp-036, exp-043, exp-036b; D060 new data"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    tables: [tab3_independence, tab4_extraction_taxonomy]
    figures: [fig3_k_sensitivity]

  - section: discussion
    file: discussion.tex
    word_budget: 500
    phase: 2
    core_bullets:
      - "Oracle causally isolates bottleneck: aggregation sound, extraction binding"
      - "Condorcet interpretation: Eff-K < 2 → constraints inherit trace non-independence"
      - "9 remediation failures confirm structural nature — not addressable by prompting, architecture, diversity, or filtering"

# Entropy-Conditioned Analysis: exp-038 (Qwen2.5-14B LogiQA-200)

**Overall**: SICA=78.0%, SC=78.5%, Delta=-0.5pp, n=200

## Main Table

| Entropy Bin | n (%) | SC Acc | SICA Acc | Delta (pp) | Override n | Override Precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low [0, 0.5) | 150 (75.0%) | 84.0% | 84.0% | +0.0 | 0 | N/A |
| Med [0.5, 1.0) | 34 (17.0%) | 67.6% | 64.7% | -2.9 | 1 | 0.0% (0/1) |
| High [1.0, +inf) | 16 (8.0%) | 50.0% | 50.0% | +0.0 | 2 | 50.0% (1/2) |

## Additional Stats

- **Unanimous rate**: 126/200 = 63.0%
- **Avg majority fraction**: 0.913
- **Dedup ratio** (unique/total constraints): 5348/6852 = 0.781

## Entropy Distribution

| Entropy Range | Count |
|---|---|
| [0.00, 0.25) | 126 |
| [0.25, 0.50) | 24 |
| [0.50, 0.75) | 11 |
| [0.75, 1.00) | 23 |
| [1.00, 1.25) | 6 |
| [1.25, 1.50) | 8 |
| [1.50, 1.75) | 2 |

Mean=0.290, Median=0.000, Std=0.435, Max=1.730

## Override Analysis

- **Low entropy**: 0 overrides (SICA never disagrees with SC)
- **Med entropy**: 1 override, all bad (SC right -> SICA wrong)
- **High entropy**: 2 overrides, 1 good + 1 bad = net zero

Total overrides: **3 out of 200** problems (1.5%)

## Cross-Experiment Comparison

| Metric | Qwen14B FOLIO-204 (exp-026) | Mistral-7B FOLIO-204 (exp-033) | Qwen14B LogiQA-200 (exp-038) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overall SICA | 85.3% | 70.1% | 78.0% |
| Overall SC | 84.8% | 67.2% | 78.5% |
| Overall Delta | +0.5pp | +2.9pp | -0.5pp |
| Low entropy n% | ~90% | 64.2% | 75.0% |
| Low entropy delta | +0.0pp | +0.0pp | +0.0pp |
| High entropy n% | 10.3% | 35.8% | 8.0% |
| High entropy delta | +4.8pp | +9.6pp | +0.0pp |
| Unanimous rate | - | - | 63.0% |

## Key Findings

1. **Low entropy = no difference**: Consistent with FOLIO findings. When SC votes are near-unanimous, SICA adds nothing (and correctly avoids overriding).

2. **High entropy provides no benefit on LogiQA**: Unlike FOLIO where high-entropy bins showed +4.8pp (Qwen) and +9.6pp (Mistral), LogiQA shows +0.0pp. Only 2 overrides in this bin, with 1 good and 1 bad canceling out.

3. **Extremely few overrides**: Only 3/200 (1.5%) problems have SICA != SC. On FOLIO, SICA overrode more frequently. This suggests the constraint extraction on LogiQA is less effective at producing discriminative signals.

4. **Mass distribution**: 75% low-entropy (between FOLIO-Mistral's 64% and FOLIO-Qwen's 90%). Only 8% high-entropy problems, a small pool where SICA could theoretically help.

5. **Net negative**: The single bad override in the medium-entropy bin accounts for the overall -0.5pp delta. SICA's constraint signal on LogiQA is too weak to overcome SC.

# Task: Write analysis.tex for the SICA paper

Write the Analysis section (§5) for the paper "Beyond Self-Consistency: How Trace Independence Limits Symbolic Consensus in LLM Reasoning". This is an EMNLP 2026 analysis paper about why symbolic constraint aggregation (SICA) fails to consistently improve over Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting for LLM reasoning.

**Before writing, you MUST**:
1. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/paper-writing-norms.skill.md`
2. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md`

**Output file**: Write the complete LaTeX to `/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_3/projects/symb_invariant_consensus/docs/paper/analysis.tex`

## Paper Context

The paper investigates why SICA (extracting FOL constraints from LLM reasoning traces and solving MAX-SAT via Z3) fails to consistently beat SC. The core finding is the **Independence Bottleneck**: Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence, but same-model traces are highly correlated (Fleiss' κ=0.40–0.74, Effective-K=1.20–2.22 for nominal K=12). Oracle control (+14.22pp FOLIO, +11.50pp ProofWriter) proves the aggregation mechanism works, but self-extracted constraints capture only ~35% of this ceiling. Nine remediation strategies spanning 6 dimensions all fail, confirming the bottleneck is structural.

## Section Structure (word budget: ~1500 words, ~1.5 pages)

### §5.1 Condorcet Effective-K Analysis (sec:effective-k, ~350 words)
**Data** (from comp-1 verified computation):
- Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO: κ=0.7442, Eff-K=1.306, unanimous_rate=58.3%, n=204
- Qwen2.5-14B LogiQA: κ=0.821, Eff-K=1.196, unanimous_rate=63.0%, n=200
- Mistral-7B FOLIO s123: κ=0.4122, Eff-K=2.168, unanimous_rate=14.2%, n=204
- Mistral-7B FOLIO s456: κ=0.4013, Eff-K=2.216, unanimous_rate=14.2%, n=204
- Mistral-7B LogiQA: κ=0.5034, Eff-K=1.836, unanimous_rate=20.5%, n=200
- Mistral-7B ICL-Oracle FOLIO: κ=0.3946, Eff-K=2.247, n=199
- Qwen2.5-14B PW-600: κ=0.6209, Eff-K=1.533, n=508
- Qwen3-14B PW-600: κ=0.7661, Eff-K=1.273, n=322
- Formula: Eff-K = K / (1 + (K-1)·κ), where κ = Fleiss' Kappa

**Key points**:
- Present Table 3 (tab:independence) with columns: Model, Domain, κ, Eff-K, Unanimous (%), SICA Δ (pp)
- Include Mistral s123 and s456 as separate rows to show cross-seed κ stability
- Cross-seed κ stable (0.412 vs 0.401) but Δ unstable (+3.43 vs -0.49pp) → Eff-K necessary not sufficient
- Correlation: higher Eff-K associates with more room for SICA gain
- Explains SC plateau: K=12 traces provide only 1.2–2.2 independent votes

### §5.2 Extraction Error Taxonomy (sec:extraction-taxonomy, ~250 words)
**Data** (from exp-023):
- Z3 semantic discriminative rate: 8.2% [95% CI: 7.6, 8.8] (out of total constraints)
- Source-trace discriminative by weight: 39.2%; by count: 12.1%
- 56.4% of cross-answer constraint pairs share zero Z3 variables (from exp-036b)
- Variable naming inconsistency is a key mechanism
- Even filtering to keep only discriminative constraints provides zero accuracy gain
- n=804 (FOLIO-204 + ProofWriter-600), model=Qwen2.5-14B

**Key points**: Most constraints are non-discriminative. The ~8% that are Z3-discriminative still fail to help because variable naming inconsistency prevents Z3 from relating constraints across traces.

### §5.3 K Sensitivity (sec:k-sensitivity, ~250 words)
**Data** (Mistral-7B FOLIO-204, seed=42):
- K=4: Δ=-1.47pp
- K=8: Δ=-0.98pp
- K=12: Δ=+4.90pp (exp-033)
- K=16: Δ=+1.47pp

**Key points**: Inverted-U curve. K=12 is sweet spot. Reference Figure 3 (\ref{fig:k-sensitivity}). At low K, insufficient constraint diversity; at high K, diminishing returns from non-independent traces. Links to Eff-K analysis.

### §5.4 Temperature Sensitivity (sec:t-sensitivity, ~100 words)
**Data**:
- T=0.7: Δ=+4.90pp (exp-033)
- T=1.0: Δ=+0.49pp (exp-054, n=204, SC=54.9%, SICA=55.4%, p=0.739)

**Key points**: Effect extremely fragile. Higher T increases diversity but degrades trace quality, collapsing the gain.

### §5.5 Entropy-Conditioned Mechanism (sec:entropy, ~200 words)
**Data** (per-problem answer entropy bins):
- Mistral-7B FOLIO (exp-033): low Δ=0pp, med Δ≈+4.5pp, high Δ=+9.6pp (monotonic)
- Proportion high-entropy problems: Mistral 35.8% vs Qwen 10.3%
- Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO (exp-026): high entropy Δ=+4.8pp but only 10.3% of problems
- Qwen2.5-14B LogiQA (exp-038): high entropy Δ=+0.0pp, only 8.0% high-entropy, 75% low-entropy
- Causal chain: strong model → consistent traces → low entropy → redundant constraints → no gain

**Key points**: Answer entropy mediates SICA effectiveness. The aggregate Δ is driven by the high-entropy subpopulation. Strong models have few high-entropy problems, limiting SICA's operating range.

### §5.6 Constraint Ablation (sec:ablation, ~100 words)
**Data** (sica_constraint_ablation_013, Qwen2.5-14B, n=804):
- MAX-SAT accuracy: 76.49% (615/804)
- Count-only accuracy: 76.62% (616/804)
- Random-weight accuracy: 75.87% (610/804)
- SC baseline: 76.24% (613/804)
- MAX-SAT vs count-only agreement: 803/804

**Key points**: Z3 solver adds essentially nothing over simple counting. Confirms degeneration equation (Eq. 4 in method.tex, eq:degenerate).

### §5.7 Remediation Analysis (sec:remediation, ~250 words)
**Data** (9 strategies, 6 dimensions, ALL fail):
1. Contrastive prompting (exp-029): disc_rate 8.2%→6.0%, Δ=-1.1pp
2. Cross-model extraction (exp-030): 0% discriminative, Δ=0pp
3. Generational scaling Qwen3 (exp-027): +0.49pp n.s.
4. Z3 feedback (exp-036): 0.9% UNSAT trigger rate, real impact=0
5. Cross-trace UNSAT (exp-036b): 56.4% zero shared vars
6. Consistency filtering (exp-043): reverts to SC at threshold≥4 (avg filtered constraints: T≥4→1.8/problem, T≥8→0.3/problem)
7. Discriminative filtering: 0 gain
8. T=1.0 diversity (exp-054): Δ collapses +4.90→+0.49pp
9. Multi-temp sampling (exp-055): n=204, Δ=0.00pp, SC=57.84%, SICA=57.84%

**Key points**: 1-paragraph summary in main text. Reference appendix table (tab:remediation in appendix). Organize by dimension: prompting, architecture, capability, verification, diversity, filtering. Conclude: all six intervention dimensions fail → bottleneck is structural, not addressable by prompt/solver/diversity changes alone.

## Cross-references to use
- Method section: §3 (sec:method), Eq. 1 (eq:effk), Eq. 2 (eq:maxsat), Eq. 3 (eq:score), Eq. 4 (eq:degenerate), Eq. 5 (eq:c0-def)
- Experiments: §4 (sec:experiments), Table 1 (tab:main_results), Figure 2 (fig:regime-scatter), §4.2 (sec:main-results), §4.4 (sec:replication)
- Figure 3 is already generated at: `artifacts/figures/paper/f3_k_sensitivity.pdf`, use `\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f3_k_sensitivity}` (graphicspath already configured)
- Appendix references: Table for remediation (tab:remediation), Table for entropy (tab:entropy_conditioned), Table for oracle subtypes (tab:pw_oracle_subtype)

## Writing Style Rules (CRITICAL)
- NO em-dashes (—) or explanatory en-dashes (–). Use commas, parentheses, or separate sentences instead.
- NO -ing phrase endings ("..., demonstrating that...")
- NO "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally" chains
- NO "It is worth noting" / "Notably"
- NO "leverage" / "utilize" / "delve into" / "a myriad of"
- Tight, direct prose. Academic but not flowery.
- Every number must come from the data above. Do not invent numbers.
- Use `\S` for section references (e.g., `\S\ref{sec:main-results}`)
- Keep paragraphs 5-8 sentences. Do not over-fragment.
- No comments in LaTeX unless explaining a non-obvious constraint.

## Already-written sections for cross-reference consistency

**method.tex** key labels: sec:method, sec:condorcet, sec:pipeline, sec:oracle-design, sec:scope, eq:effk, eq:maxsat, eq:score, eq:degenerate, eq:c0-def, fig:pipeline
**experiments.tex** key labels: sec:experiments, sec:exp-setup, sec:main-results, sec:oracle, sec:replication, sec:failure-modes, tab:main_results, fig:regime-scatter

The experiments.tex already covers failure modes (Type A/B/C) in §4.5. The analysis section deepens these with quantitative mechanisms. Do not repeat the regime descriptions; instead, reference §4.5 and explain WHY each regime behaves as it does using the Eff-K/entropy/extraction data.

[Director 指令] [Patch — exp-033 κ 数据到位 + Eff-K 修正]

exp-033 (论文 primary experiment) κ 已计算完成。**同时修正第二 Worker 的 Eff-K 公式错误。**

正确公式: Eff-K = K / (1 + (K-1) × κ)

完整修正后数据（全部 6 个条件）：

| Exp | Model | Dataset | κ | Eff-K | SC% | Δpp | p |
|-----|-------|---------|---|-------|-----|-----|---|
| exp-033 | Mistral-7B | FOLIO s42 | 0.500 | **1.85** | 54.41 | +4.90 | 0.013 |
| exp-052 | Mistral-7B | FOLIO s123 | 0.412 | 2.17 | 53.92 | +3.43 | 0.039 |
| exp-053 | Mistral-7B | FOLIO s456 | 0.401 | 2.22 | 56.37 | -0.49 | 1.0 |
| exp-046 | Mistral-7B | PW-600 | 0.210 | **3.63** | 39.33 | -2.83 | 0.010 |
| exp-026 | Qwen-14B | FOLIO | 0.744 | 1.31 | 75.49 | +0.25 | n.s. |
| exp-038 | Qwen-14B | LogiQA | 0.821 | 1.20 | 78.50 | -0.50 | n.s. |

**叙事要点**：
- 跨模型：Qwen Eff-K≈1.2-1.3 → 0 gain；Mistral Eff-K≈1.85-2.22 → variable gain → Eff-K 是跨模型必要条件
- exp-046 Eff-K 最高(3.63) 但 SC 太低(39%) → delta 为负 → 需同时满足 sufficient Eff-K AND sufficient SC
- Mistral seeds 内部 Eff-K 与 delta 非单调（exp-033 Eff-K 最低但 delta 最高）→ seed variance 主导

writing_plan.yaml 和 plots 中涉及 Eff-K 的地方都需要用这些修正值。paper_framing.md 已更新。
